v.why: Raising an already large Adam step size (0.08-1) causes divergence and accuracy collapse, unlike raising a small one.
At tiny learning rates the model is under-trained, so a larger step improves convergence within 243 epochs.
Lowering a divergent learning rate recovers stable training, giving large gains compared with lowering a moderate one.
With a tiny learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and worse underfitting.
Smaller batches add more update steps, which matters most when each step is tiny.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at aggressive learning rates.
Tiny batches combined with larger steps yield very noisy, unstable updates.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty (0.13 to 1) causes heavy underfitting, while increasing a negligible one has no effect.
Adding units to a narrow network relieves a capacity bottleneck, whereas gains saturate for wide networks.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units at high learning rates.

raw:
Without running anything, I based these on known MLP training behavior: Adam diverges at high learning rates, a run can be update-starved when the learning rate is small and batches are large, strong L2 penalties hurt, and extra width helps most when the network is narrow.
